content:
Laredo's District 2 City Council race is a rematch with a contested history — and two very different pitches for what the district needs most. Incumbent Ricardo “Richie” Rangel Jr. and former Councilwoman Daisy Campos-Rodriguez are on the November 3 ballot, and both laid out their priorities this week as early voting entered its final days, according to KGNS.

Rangel, described as a lifelong District 2 resident, puts water infrastructure at the top of his list, alongside more commercial growth and closer work with economic development efforts. Campos-Rodriguez, who grew up in the district and serves as an assistant director for Webb County Public Health Services, wants to refocus on basic neighborhood services: streets, speed humps, sidewalks and parks.

The rematch carries baggage from 2022. Campos-Rodriguez was initially declared the winner of that contest by six votes, but after a 2023 civil lawsuit over alleged illegal ballots, a judge found that 15 people who voted for her had improperly established residency and awarded the seat to Rangel. The Texas Supreme Court denied her appeal in January 2024, according to KGNS.

Early voting in Webb County ends Friday, October 30, at 8 p.m. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, with polls open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. District 2 is one of four Laredo council seats on the ballot this year, along with Districts 1, 3 and 6, plus the mayor's race and Municipal Court Judge Place 1.

What to watch next: which pitch wins over District 2 voters — the incumbent's infrastructure-and-growth agenda or the challenger's back-to-basics neighborhood plan — and whether the race is close enough to head to a December runoff.

Sources:

  • KGNS, "District 2 candidates outline priorities as early voting continues," October 29, 2026

title: Laredo District 2: Rangel bets on water and growth, Campos-Rodriguez on streets and parks
